transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maria (CTO), Samir (Lead DevOps), Evan (Security), Lena (Data Platform), Tom (ML)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot health: networking validation still blocking full benchmark, small perf wins after kernel tweak, discussed runtime upgrade next week and fallbacks. Agreed next steps: shared security pack, confirm VPC CIDRs, schedule upgrade window, run 24h perf test.

Topics:
- Networking / VPC peering status
- Routing & NAT, egress for telemetry
- Runtime upgrade and model variant routing
- Pilot perf numbers and tuning
- Next steps and compliance docs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick 45 min sync, agenda is net routing, upgrade, results review and next steps; feel free to interrupt.
[00:18] Maria: thanks jordan, yep we wanted to focus on the firewall peering stuff and then the perf numbers you sent, a few folks from infra and security here.
[00:28] Samir: yeah quick status from our side, we flagged the peering request yesterday but we saw some overlap with existing route tables, so we held off, i can share the screenshot, but basically the route table in the analytics subnet has a more specific route that supersedes the peering, so traffic to the Redwood private subnets is getting blackholed.
[00:46] Priya: okay that explains why the probes were failing; on our side the initial connectivity test showed TLS handshake success but no egress for the health probes, so we couldn't finish the tail latency runs.
[01:04] Tom: can you remind us which ports/protocols the probes use? we opened 443 only, should we add anything else?
[01:12] Priya: we use HTTPS (443) for the control plane and a separate ephemeral port range for health/kv cache warmup - usually ephemeral ephemeral-high ports, but the important bit is the egress to our metrics collector and S3/obj store for model cache prefetching. if egress is blocked by NAT gateway rules, the runtime can't warm the cache so cold-start tails spike.
[01:36] Samir: i think the NAT gateway was configured to only allow 443 and 80 outbound, we can add the ephemeral range but need a business justification for that.
[01:44] Evan: from security perspective we prefer least privilege, but if you can provide the list of exact ports and CIDRs we can make a scoped rule. also please send the network diagram so we can review.
[02:00] Jordan: note, we'll share the network diagram in the security pack - it'll call out the control plane endpoints, metrics egress, and the optional S3 object store endpoints.
[02:10] Maria: thanks, that helps. next, priya you mentioned some perf wins after kernel tweaks?
[02:16] Priya: yeah so we pushed 2 small tweaks in the model runtime config - one was switching the attention kernel variant for long context sequences and the other was adjusting the kv cache prefetch policy; result was a 12% improvement in p95 token latency for the 2k context workload, cost per token unchanged. caveat: that was on a small sample with synthetic traffic because full benchmark couldn't run due to networking.
[02:46] Tom: 12% p95 is good; did you see any regression in throughput?
[02:50] Priya: throughput held steady, a little more memory churn but within headroom; we saw improved cache hit rate from ~54% to ~68% which explains latency improvement.
[03:06] Maria: are these kernel flags something you can toggle at runtime or do we need a restart?
[03:12] Priya: some are runtime flags, others require a rolling restart of the runtime process; we plan to bundle them in the upgrade next week and have a short maintenance window.
[03:20] Jordan: we should talk about the upgrade schedule - we propose target 2026-11-18 evening PDT for minimal traffic, with a canary on one host and a 30 minute observation window.
[03:30] Samir: that's feasible but need to coordinate with our change freeze windows; evening PDT is okay if we keep it under 90 minutes. what's the rollback plan?
[03:38] Priya: rollback is a simple config revert and redeploy to previous runtime image; we keep the previous kernel artifacts on the host for fast rollback, plus traffic can be routed back to hosted fallback if needed.
[03:48] Evan: hosted fallback raises data residency flags though — we prefer not to send customer traffic off-prem unless absolutely necessary, is that correct?
[03:56] Jordan: yes that's an important point — fallback to Redwood Hosted would only be an opt-in safety net and we'd mask/route sensitive traffic per the contract; for AtlasHealth we discussed staying on private only unless you approve a limited test.
[04:12] Lena: for telemetry where does observability forward to? can we keep traces internal?
[04:18] Priya: observability uses a push model to your prometheus/grafana endpoint in the VPC; logs can be streamed to your S3 or internal ELK. we do send minimal aggregated health metrics to the Redwood control plane for monitoring if you enable it, but that's opt-in and encrypted.
[04:38] Maria: perfect. ok back to blockers: samir, you'll confirm route table updates and whether you can allow ephemeral ports to the runtime hosts?
[04:46] Samir: yes i will, but one more ask — we want to limit egress to specific S3 endpoints. will the runtime accept a fixed list of S3 region endpoints?
[04:56] Priya: yes we can provide a list of S3 endpoints and an alternate path using an internal object cache if you'd rather avoid public S3 access; we'll include those in the security pack.
[05:08] Tom: any visibility on token burn / cost numbers from the pilot so far?
[05:12] Jordan: summary: small sample run showed avg token cost aligns with estimate, but tail latency contributed to higher agg cost during cold caches; once the kernel + cache fixes land and we run a 24h steady-state test we expect cost-per-request to drop ~8-12%.
[05:28] Priya: to add, our batching heuristics also improved p95 when request size has tight variance; we'll tune batching on the 24h run to hit both latency and token-cost SLOs.
[05:40] Maria: sounds good. any security Qs left? Evan?
[05:44] Evan: a couple - KMS integration for model keys and audit log retention, do you have an HSM/KMS integration guide? also need an SLA matrix for private deployment.
[05:56] Jordan: yes we'll include KMS/HSM notes in the security pack and the SLA doc. expect that in the package we send by Friday (2026-11-13).
[06:06] Maria: perfect. last thing — routing and canary. if the canary fails do we have automatic traffic split back to previous image?
[06:14] Priya: we have canary rollouts configurable; policy can auto-failover to previous host and optionally shift traffic to a compatible model variant or the hosted fall back. we'll provide the exact policy templates.
[06:28] Samir: when you say compatible variant, do you mean quantized model variant? our infra team is worried about output drift with quantized models.
[06:36] Priya: yes, compatible often means a model variant using a different quantization profile but same architecture; we run evals on a small prompt set before enabling route. for AtlasHealth we'd limit any fallback to variants that pass the eval threshold you define.
[06:54] Tom: ok good. can you share the eval prompt set and thresholds?
[06:58] Jordan: we will, we'll attach the prompt set (shortlist) and the eval report in the security pack link, and also the benchmark spreadsheet — link placeholder: (link: redwood/pilot/atlashealth/benchmarks)
[07:12] Maria: great. quick recap of next steps?
[07:16] Jordan: sure - redwood shares security pack + network diagram + eval prompt set by Friday; samir to confirm route table and CIDR by Friday; priya to prepare upgrade playbook and run 24h perf test week of 11/16; jordon to update pricing for dedicated fallback scenarios.
[07:36] Samir: i'll add that to our ticketing and update you.
[07:40] Evan: i'll compile the compliance Qs and send by EOD tomorrow.
[07:44] Jordan: awesome, thanks everyone, we'll sync next week same time unless another blocker pops up.
[07:50] Maria: thanks all.

Notes (imperfect transcription observed): occasional speaker overlap, 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'kay vee cache', 'Redwood' appears as 'red wood' in one segment.
